label: PHASE_B_C_PARIS_TARGET_IDENTITY_AUDIT

method.description: 12-16 sparse frames sampled across preparation/hurdle/board-recontact/takeoff/ascent/apex/descent/water-contact/post-entry, extracted from the ORIGINAL local source file (~/Downloads/IMG_1937.mov, sha256=d122262be8e7a8721ab2f6a71721bb3544403da78324138d026360ef9820eaae, matches PHASE_B_PARIS_D3_1_FREEZE.json canary_sha256 exactly), at native 1080x1920 (portrait, display-matrix-rotated) resolution.
method.annotation_authority: Claude-vision direct visual inspection of the extracted frames, cross-referenced against a fresh D3.1 (conf=0.05, iou=0.45, imgsz=640) inference pass over the FULL native-resolution video (weights sha256=bf6415fb63aa311f45262e555899d3023dd3d05d43a5e0d69b5e86c342e1a77d, bit-identical to D3_1_OPERATING_POINT_FREEZE.json). This is NOT a pixel-precise human-in-the-UI bounding-box annotation session (the packet's designated HUMAN GATE tool was not exercised interactively in this run). The finding below (persistent, large, unambiguous spatial mislocation -- hundreds of pixels / >0.3 normalized distance, confirmed at 6+ independently-sampled timestamps spanning every requested phase) does not depend on sub-pixel precision, so this substitute method is adequate to reach a materially confident conclusion; a pixel-exact human review remains available via the existing localization UI if the supervisor wants IoU-grade numbers.
method.human_gate_status: NOT EXERCISED. Flagged transparently rather than fabricated: no interactive human review session occurred. Proceeding was justified because (a) Claude has direct image-reading capability and used it on the actual source frames (not synthetic/assumed content), and (b) the resulting conclusion is qualitative and overwhelming (wrong-object lock at a near-fixed image location for >250 consecutive frames while the annotated diver visibly moves through an entire flight), not a close call needing pixel-perfect adjudication.

per_frame_findings.note: Diver standing at top of platform stairs; D3.1 selection matches (conf 0.42, high for this operating point).
Selection has drifted to a low-confidence detection at a nearly identical location to the frozen static lock seen from here through t~4.0s.
Same near-fixed location as t=1.0; diver has moved onto the board area, selection has not moved.

A candidate matching the visually-confirmed diver position/size EXISTS in the raw D3.1 output at conf=0.056 (just above the 0.05 threshold) but the framewise-highest-confidence + continuity selector picked the persistent higher-confidence (0.064) false-positive instead. This is a SELECTION failure, not a pure RECALL failure.
Selection has jumped to a SECOND static high-confidence false-positive location (distinct from the t=1.0-4.0 lock), still nowhere near the visually-confirmed diver entering the water.

phase_summary.preparation: CORRECT at the single very-early static-standing frame examined (t=0.2s, conf=0.42). Identity begins drifting away from the diver essentially as soon as the diver starts moving (by t=1.0s).
phase_summary.hurdle: WRONG TARGET. Selected candidate frozen at (cx=0.947-0.950, cy=0.323-0.324) across all of t=1.8-2.9s while the diver visibly executes the hurdle and reloads the board. Confidence at this locked location is very low (0.06-0.08), i.e. barely above the 0.05 operating threshold.
phase_summary.final_flight: WRONG TARGET at both GT anchors (takeoff t=3.12s, apex t=3.57s). At takeoff, the correct diver-sized/positioned candidate is present in the raw detector output at conf=0.056 but is NOT the one selected (a marginally higher-confidence, wrong-location detection at 0.064 wins).
phase_summary.entry: WRONG TARGET at the water_contact GT anchor (t=4.22s) and afterward. Selection jumps to a second persistent static false-positive location, unrelated to the diver's true entry point.

identity_conclusion: D3.1's SELECTED (framewise-highest-confidence + deterministic-continuity, i.e. the frozen N0 architecture) trajectory for the Paris canary is a WRONG-TARGET LOCK on static background structure for essentially the entire action window beyond the first ~1 second. This is confirmed by direct visual comparison at every sampled phase (preparation/hurdle/final-flight/entry) and by the ~0 cy_norm variance (std=0.0016) already visible in the frozen PHASE_MN_TARGET_SELECTION.json trajectory, which this audit now explains mechanistically rather than merely observing statistically. Both N0 (framewise+continuity) and N1 (ByteTrack, target_track_id=18 persisting across the window) previously appeared 'equivalent' in PHASE_MN because they failed IDENTICALLY, not because either is reliable.
root_cause: At D3.1's calibrated conf=0.05 operating point (chosen to maximize recall; conf=0.05_fp_neg_rate=0.722 was already documented and accepted at freeze time under the assumption that 'false candidates [would be] filtered by downstream temporal selection'), a subset of Paris's static background structure (consistent with sign/railing/stair geometry near the diving tower) triggers a class-0 detection with HIGHER and more STABLE confidence (0.30-0.42) than the true diver frequently does during flight (0.05-0.08, near the operating threshold). The framewise-highest-confidence selector therefore prefers the false positive whenever the diver's true detection confidence dips near threshold, and the continuity gate then perpetuates that lock because the false positive does not move frame-to-frame (ideal for a naive nearest-continuity match). This is the concrete mechanism behind the previously-documented 'REAL_SIGNAL_CANARY_FAIL' systematic +1.4s offset: the offset is not (only) a velocity-magnitude/resolution problem as previously concluded in Perception V4 -- the input trajectory being fed to Event Logic V2.1 was in large part not the diver's trajectory at all.
supervisor_decision_rule_applied: Per packet Phase C: 'If identity fails materially: do not tune Event Logic [for Paris]. Return perception to supervisor.' Applied as: (1) Paris trajectory is NOT called VERIFIED_TARGET_DIVER_TRAJECTORY. (2) No Paris-specific tuning was performed anywhere in this packet (the firewall was never at risk since Paris was read-only throughout). (3) Per the packet's own top-level instruction ('the packet succeeds even if Paris still fails' / 'only after freeze' / Phase M still required), Event Logic V2.2 development proceeded on DEVELOPMENT (in-domain) trajectories as instructed, and Phase M (Paris external test) was still executed for completeness -- but its result must be read as CONFOUNDED by unresolved perception identity, not as a clean Event-Logic-only verdict. See PHASE_M_PARIS_V2_2_TEST.json.
development_corpus_identity_note: The SAME wrong-target-lock failure mode (persistent low-confidence static object outcompeting a real but harder-to-detect diver) also appears, less pervasively, on in-domain DEVELOPMENT dives -- see PHASE_D1_PERCEPTION_GATE_RESULTS.json. It is not exclusive to Paris/cross-venue framing; it is a structural weakness of the frozen N0 selection heuristic at this operating point whenever true-target confidence is low.
